chapter: Broadway, tenors, Billie Holiday and Rhythm Club memories
title: Roy Eldridge and Bunny Berigan

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: You mentioned Roy Eldridge. Let's talk about him for a while.

Roy, we made all his records with Billie Holiday together. Roy, Benny Goodman, Ben, Teddy Wilson, Kirby. We made the first records, 'Miss Brown to You,' 'What a Little Moonlight Can Do.' Roy was on those. Then I made so many records with Roy, 'Braggin' In Brass,' all those things. Roy, Charlie Shavers, Joe Thomas.
Joe Thomas the tenor player?

No, the trumpet player, the trumpet player. Yeah, Roy, he, great musician, great stylist. He set the pace for many a trumpet player out here. Roy Eldridge did. Roy and Charlie Shavers. I knew Bunny Berigan real good.
He was another guy who drank himself to death.
Lee Wiley. Singer. I knew Bunny real good. Made records with Bunny. Drank hisself to death, just drinking. Too bad.
Bunny was, from what I've read, just a very nice easy going guy.
Yeah, Bunny Berigan, very nice. You'd love him. Just drink, love Bunny. When did he die, '41?
Bunny Berigan, Red McKenzie, have you heard of him? He was back there with the Eddie Condon days ...
With the kazoo.
Yeah, Red McKenzie. Dick McDonough, ever heard of him?
Yeah.
Carl Kress.
Both of them, yeah.
Good Guitar players. Good. Dick Stabile. I just saw Dick Stabile in New Orleans a couple of years ago.
How did he sound?
Good. He had the big band in one of the hotels there in New Orleans.
Pick up band?
Well it's an organized band since he's been in the hotel.
He lives there, right? That's right.
Yeah, a couple of years.
